hook: Meet Cassy, a sketched young woman who lives on paper and talks through sign language and writing. The article is short and gentle, but keep its bittersweet tag in mind as you go. Pay attention to what the Foundation chooses to give her, and what it holds back.
whyItMatters: SCP-085 is tagged foundation-made: she exists because researchers ran a drawing made with SCP-067 through SCP-914, so the file links straight into two other objects. It is a Safe, sapient entry where the interest lies in a person's situation rather than in any danger. The rules about paper and fire show how much procedure can gather around someone who is mostly harmless.
thingsToNotice:
The Escher test plays as comedy: she happily walks the impossible staircase and wonders why real stairs are not built that way, which also hints that her world runs on its own logic. The incident report is the emotional center. To spare her distress, the Foundation had told her she was the last human alive in a post-apocalyptic world, writing off any oddities as dreams, until a researcher carelessly carried a printed copy of her own containment procedures into the room and she slipped onto it and read the truth.

The aftermath is plain: several researchers wanted her destroyed, the O5 Council narrowly let her live, and she now shows signs of clinical depression that therapy may not reach. The Mustang project is the closing image, a year spent moving parts from technical drawings into another picture and building a car by hand, fueled from a Norman Rockwell gas-station print. Every such diversion still waits on O5 approval, which quietly measures how much kindness the institution can manage.

related.note: Running her sketch through this machine on Fine is what brought her to life.
